blocks.text: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI, 1935)** is the **central bank** — banker to the government, issuer of currency, and manager of **monetary policy** to control inflation and support growth, now under a **flexible inflation-targeting** framework.

rows: Central bank; nationalised **1949**; functions — currency issue, banker's bank, monetary policy, forex, regulator.
**MPC (6 members)** sets the **repo rate**; targets **CPI inflation 4% ±2%**.
**Repo & reverse repo, CRR, SLR, MSF, OMO, Bank Rate**.
**Dear money (contractionary)** to curb inflation; **cheap money (expansionary)** to boost growth.
Flexible IT framework since **2016** (RBI Act amended).

items: RBI (1935, nationalised 1949); MPC sets repo rate; CPI target 4% ±2%.
Tools: repo, CRR, SLR, MSF, OMO; raising repo/CRR = contractionary.

prelimsPointers: **RBI established 1935** (Hilton-Young Commission); **nationalised 1949**; HQ Mumbai.
**Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** — **6 members** (3 RBI + 3 govt-nominated); sets the **repo rate**.
Inflation target — **CPI 4% (±2%)** since 2016.
**Quantitative tools** — **Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR, MSF, Bank Rate, OMO**.
**CRR** (cash reserve ratio) & **SLR** (statutory liquidity ratio) — reserve requirements.
Raising **repo/CRR** = **contractionary (dear money)**; lowering = expansionary.
RBI is the **sole issuer of currency** (except one-rupee notes/coins by the Finance Ministry).
mainsAngles: Explain the tools of RBI's monetary policy and inflation targeting.

glossary.definition: The rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks; the key monetary-policy lever.
Cash Reserve Ratio — the share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI.
The Monetary Policy Committee that sets the repo rate to meet the inflation target.

sections.heading: Banking & financial-sector reforms; commercial banks & NPAs

blocks.text: India's **banking system** — led by public-sector banks after **nationalisation (1969)** — has undergone major **reforms (Narasimham Committees)**, and today grapples with **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)** while expanding **financial inclusion**.

rows: **14 banks in 1969, 6 in 1980**; expanded rural banking.
**(1991 & 1998)** — banking-sector reforms (prudential norms, capital adequacy, autonomy).
Loans not repaid (>90 days); addressed via **SARFAESI Act, IBC (2016), asset reconstruction, recapitalisation**.
**Scheduled commercial banks (public, private, foreign, RRBs), cooperative banks, SFBs, payment banks**.
**Jan Dhan, business correspondents, differentiated banks, UPI/digital**.

items: NPA resolution: SARFAESI, IBC 2016, recapitalisation; NPA = overdue >90 days.

prelimsPointers: **Bank nationalisation** — **14 banks (1969), 6 more (1980)** under Indira Gandhi.
**Narasimham Committee I (1991) & II (1998)** — financial/banking-sector reforms.
**NPA (Non-Performing Asset)** — a loan overdue beyond **90 days**.
NPA tools — **SARFAESI Act (2002), Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code (IBC, 2016), asset reconstruction companies, recapitalisation**.
Bank types — **public-sector, private, foreign, RRBs, cooperative, Small Finance & Payment Banks**.
**Basel norms** — capital-adequacy (CRAR) standards.
**UPI, Jan Dhan, business correspondents** drive financial inclusion.
mainsAngles: Discuss the problem of NPAs and banking-sector reforms in India.

glossary.definition: A Non-Performing Asset — a loan on which interest/principal is overdue beyond 90 days.
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (2016) providing a time-bound resolution of bad debts.
The committees (1991, 1998) that shaped India's banking-sector reforms.

sections.heading: Financial markets, instabilities, stock exchanges & SEBI

blocks.text: **Financial markets** channel savings to investment through the **money market (short-term)** and **capital market (long-term)**. India's **stock exchanges (BSE, NSE)** are regulated by **SEBI**, guarding against instability and protecting investors.

rows: Short-term (<1 yr) — **T-bills, call money, commercial paper, certificates of deposit**; RBI-regulated.
Long-term — **equity & debt (shares, bonds, debentures)**; primary (IPO) & secondary markets.
**Securities & Exchange Board of India** — regulator of the securities market; statutory 1992.
**Bubbles, crashes, scams (Harshad Mehta 1992)**; SEBI ensures transparency.

items: Money market (short-term, RBI) vs capital market (long-term, SEBI).

prelimsPointers: **Money market** — short-term (<1 yr): **Treasury bills, call money, commercial paper, CDs**; regulated by **RBI**.
**Capital market** — long-term: shares, bonds, debentures; **primary (IPO)** & **secondary** markets.
**BSE** — Asia's oldest exchange (1875); index **Sensex (30 stocks)**.
**NSE** — index **Nifty (50 stocks)**.
**SEBI** — established 1988, statutory since **1992**; regulator of the securities market.
**Harshad Mehta scam (1992)** led to SEBI's statutory empowerment.
**FPIs/FIIs** invest in Indian markets; **demat** accounts (NSDL/CDSL) hold securities.
mainsAngles: Distinguish the money and capital markets and explain SEBI's role.

glossary.definition: The Securities and Exchange Board of India, statutory regulator of the securities market (1992).
The market for short-term (under one year) funds, regulated by the RBI.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index of 30 large companies.

sections.heading: Tax system, recent changes & GST impact

blocks.text: India's **tax system** comprises **direct taxes (income, corporate)** and **indirect taxes**, the latter now unified under the **Goods and Services Tax (GST, 2017)** — a landmark 'One Nation, One Tax' reform administered by the **GST Council**.

rows: **Income tax, corporate tax**; progressive; burden not shiftable; **CBDT**.
Now mostly **GST**; earlier excise, VAT, service tax; **CBIC**.
**101st Amendment**; subsumed most indirect taxes; **CGST + SGST + IGST**; slabs 0/5/12/18/28%.
**Article 279A**; Union FM + state FMs; recommends rates (cooperative federalism).
**Unified market, reduced cascading, higher compliance; revenue-sharing debates**.

items: Direct (income/corporate, CBDT) vs indirect (GST, CBIC); GST via 101st Amendment (2017).
GST Council (Art 279A); CGST+SGST+IGST; removes tax cascading.

prelimsPointers: **Direct taxes** — income & corporate tax (**CBDT**); **indirect taxes** — GST (**CBIC**).
**GST launched 1 July 2017** via the **101st Constitutional Amendment**.
GST components — **CGST (centre), SGST (state), IGST (inter-state)**.
GST slabs — **0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%** (+ cess on luxury/sin goods).
**GST Council (Article 279A)** — chaired by Union FM; recommends rates.
GST subsumed **excise, service tax, VAT, octroi** etc. — 'One Nation, One Tax'.
Items outside GST — **petroleum, alcohol, electricity** (for now).
mainsAngles: Assess the impact of GST on India's tax system and federalism.

glossary.definition: The Goods and Services Tax (2017), a unified indirect tax replacing many central and state levies.
The Article 279A body of Union and state finance ministers that decides GST rates.
A tax (like income tax) borne directly by the person on whom it is levied.

blocks.text: India's **fiscal federalism** divides taxation and spending between the Centre and States (Part XII), with the **Finance Commission** periodically recommending the **sharing of taxes and grants** — the key mechanism of vertical and horizontal fiscal balance.

rows: Constituted every **5 years**; recommends **tax devolution & grants-in-aid**.
**15th FC** — states get **41%** of the divisible pool of central taxes.
**Vertical** (Centre-to-states share); **horizontal** (among states, by formula — population, area, income distance, etc.).

items: Finance Commission (Art 280, every 5 yrs); 15th FC gives states 41% of divisible pool.
Vertical vs horizontal devolution; formula factors (population, income distance, area).

prelimsPointers: **Finance Commission — Article 280**; constituted every **5 years** by the President.
First FC chaired by **K.C. Neogy**; **15th FC** by **N.K. Singh**.
**15th Finance Commission** — states' share = **41%** of the divisible pool (reduced 1% for J&K/Ladakh UTs).
**Vertical devolution** (Centre→states) & **horizontal** (among states by formula).
Horizontal formula factors — **income distance, population (2011), area, forest & ecology, demographic performance, tax effort**.
**Grants-in-aid — Article 275**.
GST Council handles indirect-tax revenue sharing (complements FC).
mainsAngles: Discuss the role of the Finance Commission in Centre-State fiscal relations.

glossary.definition: The Article 280 body recommending Centre-State tax sharing every five years.
The portion of central taxes shared with the states as recommended by the Finance Commission.
The division of taxation and spending powers between the Centre and the States.

sections.heading: Public debt, expenditure, fiscal policy & the Budget

blocks.text: **Fiscal policy** — the government's use of **taxation, expenditure and borrowing** — is expressed in the annual **Union Budget**. Key concerns are the **fiscal deficit, public debt sustainability, and FRBM discipline**.

rows: 'Annual Financial Statement'; **Revenue & Capital** accounts; presented on **1 February**.
Internal + external borrowings; sustainability = debt/GDP ratio.
Targets fiscal prudence (fiscal deficit ~3% of GDP goal).

items: Fiscal deficit = total borrowing; primary deficit = fiscal – interest; FRBM Act 2003.
Budget (Art 112) = revenue + capital accounts; presented 1 Feb.

prelimsPointers: **Union Budget** = **Annual Financial Statement (Article 112)**; presented on **1 February**.
Budget has **Revenue Account & Capital Account**.
**Fiscal deficit** = total expenditure – total receipts (excl. borrowings) = **total borrowing**.
**Revenue deficit** = revenue expenditure – revenue receipts; **Primary deficit** = fiscal deficit – interest payments.
**FRBM Act (2003)** — Fiscal Responsibility & Budget Management (deficit-reduction targets).
**Public debt** — internal (dominant) + external borrowings.
**Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account** — the three government funds.
mainsAngles: Explain fiscal policy, deficits and the FRBM framework.

glossary.definition: The gap between total expenditure and total receipts excluding borrowings — i.e. total borrowing.
The 2003 law mandating fiscal discipline and deficit-reduction targets.
The fiscal deficit minus interest payments, showing current fiscal stance.
